# CodeRank Redis CLI Demonstration Guide

This guide compiles the exact `redis-cli` commands used to inspect, demonstrate, and debug every feature of CodeRank during the DBMS defense or presentation.

---

## 1. Registration, OTP & Expiration (String + Hash + TTL)

```bash
# 1. Inspect unverified registration staged in Redis Hash
redis-cli HGETALL pending:alice@test.edu

# 2. Check remaining time-to-live (TTL) on pending registration (10 min initial)
redis-cli TTL pending:alice@test.edu

# 3. Retrieve the 6-digit OTP code generated by backend
redis-cli GET otp:alice@test.edu

# 4. Check OTP remaining validity (5 min / 300s initial)
redis-cli TTL otp:alice@test.edu

# 5. Clean up expired test keys
redis-cli DEL pending:alice@test.edu otp:alice@test.edu
```

---

## 2. Rate Limiting & Brute-Force Lockout (Atomic Counters + TTL)

```bash
# 1. Check OTP resend attempts counter (max 3 allowed per 10m)
redis-cli GET rl:otp:alice@test.edu
redis-cli TTL rl:otp:alice@test.edu

# 2. Check failed OTP guess attempts (max 5 before invalidation)
redis-cli GET rl:otpfail:alice@test.edu

# 3. Inspect IP login lockout counter (5 failed logins triggers 900s lock)
redis-cli GET rl:login:127.0.0.1

# 4. Inspect remaining lockout duration in seconds
redis-cli TTL rl:login:127.0.0.1

# 5. Manually clear IP lockout
redis-cli DEL rl:login:127.0.0.1
```

---

## 3. User Profiles & Unique Index Lookup Keys (Hash + String)

```bash
# 1. Fetch user profile Hash
redis-cli HGETALL user:1

# 2. Verify atomic unique username lookup key (SETNX)
redis-cli GET user:name:alex_code

# 3. Verify atomic unique email lookup key (SETNX)
redis-cli GET user:email:alex_code@code.edu

# 4. Check total registered users counter
redis-cli GET user:id_seq

# 5. Check usernames set membership (fallback for Bloom filter)
redis-cli SISMEMBER usernames alex_code

# 6. Check RedisBloom filter membership (when Bloom module is active)
redis-cli BF.EXISTS bf:usernames alex_code
```

---

## 4. Sessions & Sliding Expiration (Hash + TTL)

```bash
# 1. Inspect session metadata stored as a Hash
redis-cli HGETALL session:<session-token>

# 2. Verify remaining session TTL (refreshed to 3600s on each request)
redis-cli TTL session:<session-token>

# 3. Terminate a session on logout
redis-cli DEL session:<session-token>
```

---

## 5. Problem Catalog & Inverted Set Indexing (Hash + Sets)

```bash
# 1. Total problems count
redis-cli SCARD all:problems

# 2. Inspect a problem Hash record
redis-cli HGETALL problem:1

# 3. Count problems in difficulty sets
redis-cli SCARD difficulty:easy
redis-cli SCARD difficulty:medium
redis-cli SCARD difficulty:hard

# 4. Count problems in tag sets
redis-cli SCARD tag:dp
redis-cli SCARD tag:strings
redis-cli SCARD tag:arrays

# 5. Server-side Set Intersection (SINTER): Problems that are BOTH 'dp' AND 'strings'
redis-cli SINTER tag:dp tag:strings

# 6. Intersect tags AND difficulty level
redis-cli SINTER tag:dp tag:strings difficulty:medium

# 7. Server-side Set Union (SUNION): Problems that have EITHER 'geometry' OR 'bit-manipulation'
redis-cli SUNION tag:geometry tag:bit-manipulation
```

---

## 6. Submissions Queue & Consumer Groups (Streams)

```bash
# 1. Total length of the submissions stream
redis-cli XLEN submissions

# 2. Inspect active consumer groups on the submissions stream
redis-cli XINFO GROUPS submissions

# 3. Inspect individual worker instances in the judge consumer group
redis-cli XINFO CONSUMERS submissions judge-workers

# 4. Check pending (unacknowledged) messages
redis-cli XPENDING submissions judge-workers

# 5. Read the last 3 stream entries
redis-cli XREVRANGE submissions + - COUNT 3

# 6. Inspect submission Hash result
redis-cli HGETALL submission:1366

# 7. View user recent submission history List (capped to 50 via LPUSH/LTRIM)
redis-cli LRANGE user:1:history 0 9
```

---

## 7. Atomic Problem Solving & Scoring (Lua Script)

```bash
# 1. Inspect user solved set (anti-cheat deduplication set)
redis-cli SMEMBERS solved:1
redis-cli SISMEMBER solved:1 4

# 2. Inspect global leaderboard score before/after solve
redis-cli ZSCORE lb:global 1

# 3. Execute the atomic solve Lua script directly via redis-cli:
# Syntax: redis-cli EVAL "$(cat backend/src/lua/solve.lua)" 0 <userId> <problemId> <points> <contestId>
redis-cli EVAL "$(cat backend/src/lua/solve.lua)" 0 1 12 100 ""
```

---

## 8. Real-time Leaderboards (Sorted Sets / ZSETs)

```bash
# 1. View Top 10 global competitors with scores
redis-cli ZREVRANGE lb:global 0 9 WITHSCORES

# 2. View user's 0-indexed rank (Add 1 for human ranking)
redis-cli ZREVRANK lb:global 1

# 3. Query user score directly
redis-cli ZSCORE lb:global 1

# 4. University Aggregate Leaderboard (lb:college)
redis-cli ZREVRANGE lb:college 0 9 WITHSCORES

# 5. Contest-specific Leaderboard (lb:contest:1)
redis-cli ZREVRANGE lb:contest:1 0 4 WITHSCORES

# 6. Check top-100 API transient cache and TTL (5s)
redis-cli GET cache:lb:top100
redis-cli TTL cache:lb:top100
```

---

## 9. Memory-Efficient Bitmaps (Daily Coding Streaks)

```bash
# 1. Check if user 1 solved on Day 299 of 2026
redis-cli GETBIT streak:1:2026 299

# 2. Total active coding days in the year (BITCOUNT)
redis-cli BITCOUNT streak:1:2026

# 3. Set activity bit for today manually
redis-cli SETBIT streak:1:2026 300 1
```

---

## 10. HyperLogLog Cardinality Estimation (Unique Visitors)

```bash
# 1. Estimate today's unique visitors (UV)
redis-cli PFCOUNT visitors:2026-10-26

# 2. Add a visitor IP manually
redis-cli PFADD visitors:2026-10-26 192.168.1.100

# 3. Union merge past 7 days into weekly total using PFMERGE
redis-cli PFMERGE visitors:weekly_temp visitors:2026-10-26 visitors:2026-10-25
redis-cli PFCOUNT visitors:weekly_temp
redis-cli DEL visitors:weekly_temp
```

---

## 11. Security & Access Control Lists (ACL)

```bash
# 1. View all configured ACL users
redis-cli ACL LIST

# 2. View app_user rule specifications
redis-cli ACL GETUSER app_user

# 3. Test allowed command as app_user (Succeeds)
redis-cli --user app_user --pass 'AppSecret@2026' ZREVRANGE lb:global 0 2 WITHSCORES

# 4. Test blocked dangerous administrative command (Fails with NOPERM)
redis-cli --user app_user --pass 'AppSecret@2026' FLUSHALL

# 5. Test blocked unauthorized key outside allowed namespace (Fails with NOPERM)
redis-cli --user app_user --pass 'AppSecret@2026' GET unauthorized_foreign_key
```

---

## 12. Persistence & Durability (AOF + RDB)

```bash
# 1. Inspect current persistence statistics
redis-cli INFO persistence

# 2. Verify AOF is active
redis-cli CONFIG GET appendonly
redis-cli CONFIG GET appendfsync

# 3. Trigger manual AOF background compaction rewrite
redis-cli BGREWRITEAOF

# 4. Trigger manual RDB background snapshot
redis-cli BGSAVE
```

---

## 13. Eviction Policies & Memory Management

```bash
# 1. Check current memory limits and eviction policy
redis-cli CONFIG GET maxmemory
redis-cli CONFIG GET maxmemory-policy

# 2. Inspect memory usage breakdown
redis-cli INFO memory

# 3. Configure 100MB LRU eviction limit
redis-cli CONFIG SET maxmemory 100mb
redis-cli CONFIG SET maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru

# 4. Check eviction count in statistics
redis-cli INFO stats | grep evicted_keys
```

---

## 14. Replication (Port 6380 Read Replica)

```bash
# 1. Start secondary replica (from workspace root)
redis-server config/replica.conf --daemonize yes

# 2. Inspect master replication status (shows connected_slaves:1)
redis-cli -p 6379 INFO replication

# 3. Inspect replica status (shows role:slave, master_link_status:up)
redis-cli -p 6380 INFO replication

# 4. Test live write replication
redis-cli -p 6379 SET repl:demo "Replication OK"
redis-cli -p 6380 GET repl:demo

# 5. Test read-only replica protection (Blocked)
redis-cli -p 6380 SET illegal:write "fail"

# 6. Stop replica instance
redis-cli -p 6380 shutdown
```

---

## 15. Real-Time Observability & Monitoring

```bash
# 1. Live stream of all commands hitting Redis in real time (Exit with Ctrl+C)
redis-cli MONITOR

# 2. Inspect execution latency slowlog (top 10 slowest commands)
redis-cli SLOWLOG GET 10

# 3. List active client connections
redis-cli CLIENT LIST
```
